items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I stayed in a room with another boy named Lewis who had lived on Hathaway Street at one time.

ctx.x: I was 16 when I decided to leave home and my hangout was in Sinton Park with a group of other boys that had left home or had no parents and some of them had been in and out of reform school since the age of 12 years or younger.

When the weather was nice we slept anywhere we could find a place. I worked a few days at one time in a big Hotel as a bus boy and stayed in a room with another boy named Lewis who had lived on Hathaway Street at one time. We were about the same age. I didn't like the job at the Hotel so I quit. I still stayed with Lewis for a few days but one night I came to the room he wouldn't open the door for me, so I had to think of a place where I could sleep. Then I remembered that the door leading down in the cellar…

Among these homeless individuals that hung around Sinton Park at night were three boys that sang barber shop songs. As I had a voice that was not too bad, I eventually started singing with them. One whose name I remember was Jessie Seltzer, who had lost one eye and was the oldest of all. Jessie had a voice [the] like a trained singer and he used to give me voice I was to sing in the numbers. I had the baritone voice. These three boys had been singing quite a while with another fellow who was a pimp and a down…
